sentences.text: Harold Pryce is a man who lives at a house purchased in 1971 by him and his first wife, Joan, who died in 2013.
Harold Pryce lives with his second wife, Sandra, who is present in the home during the visit.
Harold Pryce and Sandra have been married for nine years.
Harold Pryce's first wife, Joan, died in 2013.
Harold Pryce's daughter, Carol, lives in Kestwick, approximately two hours away, and calls on Sundays.
The house is registered in Harold Pryce's name only.
Harold Pryce states that if he leaves the house, Sandra would take it.
Harold Pryce has a fall in the garden in the spring, which occurred before the visit.
Harold Pryce uses a stick and a frame for support when moving upstairs.
Harold Pryce can wash himself using a stool in the shower.
Harold Pryce experiences difficulty with socks, which affects his ability to dress.
Sandra cooks meals for Harold Pryce.
Harold Pryce can make a sandwich on his own.
Harold Pryce reports that Sandra keeps his medication in her handbag.
Harold Pryce does not receive his medication every day, and sometimes does not get his tablets at all.
Harold Pryce did not receive his heart tablets for three days last week.
Harold Pryce reports that he has not received his heart tablets and water tablets for several previous instances.
Harold Pryce wants to stop the abuse and wants his medication to be provided.
Harold Pryce wants Carol to be informed about the abuse and the situation with Sandra.
Harold Pryce says Carol never liked Sandra.
Harold Pryce reports that Sandra hits him with her walking stick when she gets cross.
Harold Pryce reports that Sandra hits him on his arms with her walking stick, and he raises his arms to protect himself.
Harold Pryce reports that Sandra hits him once a week, or more if she has had a bad day.
Harold Pryce reports that Sandra locks him in the bedroom when she goes out, saying it is to prevent him from falling.
Harold Pryce reports that Sandra locks him in the bedroom two or three times a week for the afternoon.
The bedroom where Harold is locked in does not have a toilet.
Harold Pryce is not in immediate danger at the time of the visit, as Sandra is going to her sister's house the next day.
Harold Pryce's pension is held in a joint account with Sandra.
Harold Pryce has his own savings book at the post office.
Sandra manages the household bills.
